problems.quote: acknowledging the need to address the issue of 'creamy layer' and disproportionate benefits within SCs
problems.problem: The Davinder Singh (2020) referral was about sub-categorisation of SCs, not creamy layer; creamy layer for SCs was addressed in Jarnail Singh (2018).
problems.correction: referring the matter to a seven-judge bench to reconsider the E.V. Chinnaiah judgment on sub-categorisation of SCs
problems.verifierReason: Davinder Singh 2020 referral was on sub-categorisation, not creamy layer; Jarnail Singh 2018 addressed creamy layer for SCs.

problems.quote: the 27 % reservation in public higher education
problems.problem: In the context of SC/ST policies (the focus of preceding paragraphs), the reservation is 22.5% (15% SC + 7.5% ST); 27% is for OBCs.
problems.correction: the 22.5 % reservation for SCs and STs in public higher education
problems.verifierReason: 27% is OBC quota; SC+ST combined is 22.5% in central higher education.

problems.quote: the 2013 amendment (FRA Amendment Act, 2013) explicitly mandates joint titling for spouses and the inclusion of unmarried daughters
problems.problem: No FRA amendment was enacted in 2013; the Forest Rights Act has not been amended to mandate joint titling for spouses or unmarried daughters.
problems.correction: the FRA has not been amended in 2013 to mandate joint titling for spouses or unmarried daughters
problems.verifierReason: No FRA Amendment Act 2013 exists; 2012 amendment didn't mandate joint titling (already in 2006 Act) or unmarried daughters.

problems.quote: Mission Karmayogi ... integrates a caste‑disaggregated leadership pipeline dashboard
problems.problem: Mission Karmayogi, launched in 2021, does not include a caste‑disaggregated leadership pipeline dashboard.
problems.correction: Mission Karmayogi does not include a caste‑disaggregated leadership pipeline dashboard
problems.verifierReason: Mission Karmayogi (2020/21) has no caste-disaggregated leadership dashboard; correction accurately negates false claim.

problems.quote: UIDAI links Aadhaar to caste certificates issued by state revenue authorities
problems.problem: UIDAI does not link Aadhaar numbers to caste certificates; such linkage is not part of official Aadhaar functionality.
problems.correction: UIDAI does not link Aadhaar to caste certificates
problems.verifierReason: UIDAI does not link/store caste data; Aadhaar has no caste field; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: Committee on the Status of Women, 1974
problems.problem: Wrong date: the Committee on the Status of Women in India was constituted in 1971, not 1974. The report "Towards Equality" was submitted in 1974.
problems.correction: Committee on the Status of Women (1971), Towards Equality report (1974)
problems.verifierReason: Committee constituted in 1971; report submitted 1974. Quote misstates committee year.

problems.quote: the Council of Trent (1545‑1563), which clarified doctrine, reformed clerical discipline and established the Index of Prohibited Books
problems.problem: The Council of Trent did not establish the Index of Prohibited Books; it was created by Pope Paul IV in 1559.
problems.correction: the Council of Trent (1545‑1563), which clarified doctrine and reformed clerical discipline; the Index of Prohibited Books was established by the Pope in 1559
problems.verifierReason: Original wrongly credits Council of Trent with establishing Index; correction correctly attributes to Pope in 1559.

problems.quote: James Watt’s separate‑condenser steam engine (1776) provided reliable rotary motion
problems.problem: Watt's separate condenser was invented in 1765 (patented 1769); rotary motion came later (1781). The date 1776 is incorrect.
problems.correction: James Watt’s separate‑condenser steam engine (1769) later provided reliable rotary motion
problems.verifierReason: Original date 1776 incorrect and implies immediate rotary motion; correction uses patent year 1769 and notes rotary motion came later.

problems.quote: added the category of “crimes against humanity”
problems.problem: The Tokyo Charter did not add the category of crimes against humanity; it was already defined in the Nuremberg Charter (Article 6(c)).
problems.correction: included the category of “crimes against humanity”
problems.verifierReason: Nuremberg Charter (1945) first defined crimes against humanity; Tokyo Charter (1946) included but did not add the category.

problems.quote: moving from a purely offensive posture to a doctrine of “reasonable sufficiency” by the late 1970s
problems.problem: The Soviet doctrine of “reasonable sufficiency” (razumnaya dostatochnost) was introduced under Gorbachev in the late 1980s, not the late 1970s.
problems.correction: moving from a purely offensive posture to a doctrine of “reasonable sufficiency” by the late 1980s
problems.verifierReason: "Reasonable sufficiency" (razumnaya dostatochnost) emerged under Gorbachev in the late 1980s, not the 1970s.

problems.quote: 1791 French revolutionary government to reorganise the Académie into the Institut de France
problems.problem: The Institut de France was created in 1795, not 1791.
problems.correction: 1795 French revolutionary government to reorganise the Académie into the Institut de France
problems.verifierReason: Institut de France created 1795 (Year III), not 1791; correction accurate.

problems.quote: 1789 Jay Treaty negotiations
problems.problem: The Jay Treaty was negotiated in 1794, not 1789.
problems.correction: 1794 Jay Treaty negotiations
problems.verifierReason: Jay Treaty negotiated 1794, not 1789; correction accurate.

problems.quote: 1771 Édit de Moulins
problems.problem: The Édit de Moulins dates from 1566; the 1771 edict on mortgage registration is not called that.
problems.correction: 1771 edict on mortgage registration
problems.verifierReason: Édit de Moulins was 1566; 1771 edict on mortgage registration had different name; correction accurate.

problems.quote: completed by his grandson César‑François Cassini de Thury
problems.problem: César‑François Cassini de Thury was Jacques Cassini's son, not his grandson.
problems.correction: completed by his son César‑François Cassini de Thury
problems.verifierReason: Cassini was Jacques Cassini's son, not grandson; correction fixes the error.

problems.quote: twin pillars of Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
problems.problem: The "twin pillars" policy (1969) designated Iran and Saudi Arabia as the two pillars of Gulf security; after 1979 the US did not formally apply that term to Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.
problems.correction: reliance on Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates Nixon's "twin pillars" (Iran & Saudi Arabia); correction uses accurate generic phrase.

problems.quote: the Soviet Union and China abstained rather than vetoed
problems.problem: On UNSC Resolution 678 (29 Nov 1990) the Soviet Union voted in favor; only China abstained.
problems.correction: China abstained; the Soviet Union voted yes
problems.verifierReason: UNSCR 678: USSR voted yes, China abstained; correction matches vote record.

problems.quote: Soviet losses exceeded 15,000 dead
problems.problem: Official Soviet casualties were 14,453 dead, not exceeding 15,000.
problems.correction: Soviet losses totaled about 14,500 dead
problems.verifierReason: Official Soviet Afghan war dead 14,453; "exceeded 15,000" is wrong; correction ~14,500 is accurate.

problems.quote: newly formed United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration (UNRRA)
problems.problem: UNRRA was established in 1943, not newly formed in 1947, and did not coordinate the partition relief effort.
problems.correction: United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration (UNRRA)
problems.verifierReason: UNRRA founded 1943, not 'newly formed' in 1947; correction removes inaccurate phrase.

problems.quote: ending the post‑war Bretton Woods era of cheap energy
problems.problem: The Bretton Woods monetary system ended in 1971; the oil shock ended the era of cheap energy, not the Bretton Woods era.
problems.correction: ending the post‑war era of cheap energy
problems.verifierReason: Bretton Woods was monetary, not energy; cheap energy era ended with 1973 oil shock; correction accurate.

problems.quote: championed the anti‑apartheid cause at the UN and Non‑Aligned Movement since 1946
problems.problem: Non-Aligned Movement founded in 1961, not 1946
problems.correction: championed the anti‑apartheid cause at the UN since 1946 and the Non‑Aligned Movement since 1961
problems.verifierReason: NAM founded 1961; quote incorrectly dates it to 1946; correction separates UN (1946) and NAM (1961) accurately.

problems.quote: assumed the USSR’s UN Security Council seat and nuclear arsenal under the Lisbon Protocol (May 1992) to the START I treaty
problems.problem: UN Security Council seat assumed in Dec 1991, not under Lisbon Protocol
problems.correction: assumed the USSR’s UN Security Council seat in December 1991 and its nuclear arsenal under the Lisbon Protocol (May 1992) to the START I treaty
problems.verifierReason: Russia assumed USSR UNSC seat Dec 1991; Lisbon Protocol (May 1992) covered nuclear arsenal; correction properly separates the two events.

problems.quote: later multilateralised in 2010 as the CMIM with a US$240 bn pool
problems.problem: CMIM established in 2010 with $120 bn pool; $240 bn came later
problems.correction: later multilateralised in 2010 as the CMIM with a US$120 bn pool (later expanded to $240 bn)
problems.verifierReason: CMIM launched 2010 with $120bn, doubled to $240bn in 2012; quote states $240bn in 2010; correction fixes amount and notes later expansion.

problems.quote: halted the SADF at the Battle of Quifangondo (November 1975)
problems.problem: The Battle of Quifangondo (10 November 1975) was fought between Cuban/MPLA forces and FNLA/Zairean forces; the South African Defence Force (SADF) was not the primary opponent there. SADF forces were engaged further south in Operation Savannah.
problems.correction: halted the FNLA/Zairean advance at the Battle of Quifangondo (November 1975)
problems.verifierReason: SADF was not at Quifangondo; they were halted further south at Ebo/Bridge 14. Correction correctly identifies FNLA/Zaireans as the opponent.

problems.quote: $1.1 trillion in IMF resources
problems.problem: The $1.1 trillion figure referred to a total global financial support package agreed at the London G20 summit, not solely IMF resources. The IMF portion was $500 billion (later increased to $750 billion).
problems.correction: $1.1 trillion in global financial support
problems.verifierReason: The $1.1 trillion was the total G20 London Summit package (IMF $500B, SDRs $250B, MDBs $250B, trade $100B), not IMF resources alone.
